entries.name: St. Patrick's Day
entries.capsule: Irish feast day; St. Paul holds one of the country's best-known parades, running since 1967.

dates.source: Visit Saint Paul, St. Patrick's Day 2026 page

entries.whatItMarks: The feast of St. Patrick, patron saint of Ireland; a day of Irish heritage.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: St. Paul's parade, begun in 1967, starts at noon in Mears Park and ends near Rice Park; 2026 marked its 60th anniversary. Irish Arts Minnesota has hosted a St. Patrick's Day celebration at Landmark Center for over 40 years. West Seventh Street holds tent parties, and pubs, dance schools and comedy clubs run events through March.

entries.name: Syttende Mai
entries.capsule: Norway's Constitution Day, May 17, celebrated with children's parades, flags and bunads in Minneapolis, Spring Grove and elsewhere.
entries.dateRule: May 17 each year; Minnesota events are often held on the nearest weekend.

dates.source: Fixed date; The Alley article on Mindekirken's celebration

entries.whatItMarks: The signing of Norway's constitution at Eidsvoll on May 17, 1814.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Mindekirken in Minneapolis holds a festival service, a folketog (people's parade) led by its band, games and folk dancing. Spring Grove, the state's first Norwegian settlement, holds a multi-day festival with a Grand Parade, except in decennial Homecoming years. St. Olaf alumni held a brunch at Norway House in 2026.

minnesotaEvents.name: Syttende Mai Celebration at Norway House (St. Olaf alumni)
Spring Grove Syttende Mai
minnesotaEvents.organizerDates: May 15-19, 2024 (most recent dated schedule opened); replaced by Homecoming in June 2027

sources.title: Join Mindekirken for Syttende Mai, The Alley

entries.name: Syttende Mai at Mindekirken (Minneapolis)
entries.capsule: Festival service, flag parade led by the church band, and children's games at Minneapolis's Norwegian Memorial Church.
entries.dateRule: Held on or near May 17; announced each year by Mindekirken.

dates.source: The Alley (article by a Mindekirken member); Mindekirken's own site could not be opened

entries.whatItMarks: Norwegian Constitution Day, kept by a bilingual Lutheran congregation.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: 10:30 a.m. prelude, festival worship, a folketog through the neighborhood, free hot dogs and ice cream for children, Sons of Norway Peer Gynt Dancers, Concordia Language Villages and Daughters of Norway activities.

sources.title: Join Mindekirken for Syttende Mai, The Alley

entries.name: Spring Grove Homecoming
entries.capsule: Spring Grove's once-a-decade, five-day reunion, held in place of Syttende Mai; next in June 2027.
entries.dateRule: Every ten years, in June, replacing that year's Syttende Mai.

dates.source: City of Spring Grove: 'Our next Homecoming will be June 2027' (exact days not given)

entries.whatItMarks: Alumni and friends returning to Minnesota's first Norwegian settlement.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Five days of events including the heritage foods and traditions usually seen at Syttende Mai.

sources.title: Heritage, City of Spring Grove

entries.name: Svenskarnas Dag and Midsummer
entries.capsule: Swedish midsummer festival with a raised maypole and folk dancing, held at Minnehaha Park since 1934; current status unclear.
entries.dateRule: Midsummer in late June; Svenskarnas Dag was held on a Sunday in late June. No current organizer schedule found.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Begun in 1934 at Minnehaha Park with a midsummer pole, Swedish music and dancing and a Midsummer Queen. Joined with Norway Day in 2015 as the Scandinavian Summer Fest; a third annual fest was announced for 2018. No later edition was confirmed. Sons of Norway members in Windom celebrate Mid-Solen at the solstice.

sources.title: Swedish Immigration to Minnesota, MNopedia
First Scandinavian Summer Fest, Nordstjernan

entries.name: St. Paul Oktoberfest
entries.capsule: Two-day German festival on the Germanic-American Institute's Summit Avenue grounds; its biggest yearly fundraiser.
entries.dateRule: A Friday and Saturday in September, announced each year by the Germanic-American Institute.
entries.whatItMarks: German heritage, modeled on Munich's Oktoberfest.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Music, food and beer at 301 Summit Ave., St. Paul; Friday 4-10 p.m. and Saturday 10 a.m.-10 p.m. in 2026; proceeds support German language and culture programs.

minnesotaEvents.name: St. Paul Oktoberfest
minnesotaEvents.place: Germanic-American Institute, 301 Summit Ave., St. Paul

sources.title: St. Paul Oktoberfest, Germanic-American Institute

entries.name: New Ulm Oktoberfest
entries.capsule: Two weekends of German music, food and parades across New Ulm, 'Minnesota's most German city.'
entries.dateRule: The first two weekends of October.
entries.whatItMarks: German heritage and the harvest season.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Downtown street festival Oct. 2-3, 2026, with a keg tapping and the German-American Day Parade on Minnesota Street on Saturday; events at Schell's brewery, hotels, museums and Domeier's German Store over both weekends; polka and German bands.

minnesotaEvents.name: Downtown New Ulm Oktoberfest and German-American Day Parade

entries.name: FinnFest USA
entries.capsule: National Finnish American festival, held in Minneapolis in September 2026 and planned there again in September 2027.
entries.dateRule: Announced each year by FinnFest USA; location varies.

dates.source: FinnFest 2026 program guide says a larger Minneapolis festival is planned for September 2027; days not announced

entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: 2026: programs, music, films and the free Tori Nordic fair at the Hilton Minneapolis Downtown, with Sunday at the American Swedish Institute. FinnFest has its national offices in Minneapolis and has met in Duluth and Minneapolis before.

minnesotaEvents.name: FinnFest USA 2026
minnesotaEvents.place: Hilton Minneapolis Downtown and American Swedish Institute

entries.name: St. Urho's Day
entries.capsule: Playful Finnish American holiday, the day before St. Patrick's, honoring a legendary saint who chased grasshoppers from Finland.
entries.dateRule: March 16 each year; town celebrations fall on a nearby weekend.

dates.source: Fixed date per Northern News Now and CBS Minnesota

entries.whatItMarks: Finnish American humor and heritage; the legend dates to the 1950s, and the colors are purple (grapes) and green (grasshoppers).
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Finland, Minnesota, has celebrated since 1975 with the Miss Helmi contest (since 1984), a pancake breakfast, a tug-of-war and a parade. Menahga holds a parade, coronation and 'changing of the guard.' A Finnish American historical society chapter met at a Duluth Lutheran church in 2025.

minnesotaEvents.name: St. Urho's Day celebration, Finland MN
minnesotaEvents.organizerDates: March 13-15, 2026 (as reported by North Shore Journal)

sources.title: Purple and Green to Paint Finland, North Shore Journal

entries.name: Twin Cities Irish Fest
entries.capsule: Three-day Irish music, dance and culture festival on St. Paul's Harriet Island, drawing over 30,000 people.
entries.dateRule: A Friday-Sunday weekend in early August, announced each year.

dates.source: Visit Saint Paul guide (organizer's site could not be opened)

entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Six outdoor stages, Irish dance, hurling and camogie demonstrations, a marketplace and children's activities; begun in 1980 and on Harriet Island since 2001; offers a Quiet Space for guests with autism or sensory needs.

minnesotaEvents.name: Twin Cities Irish Fest 2026
minnesotaEvents.place: Harriet Island Regional Park, St. Paul

entries.name: Kolacky Days
entries.capsule: Montgomery's late-July Czech heritage festival, crowning royalty since 1931 in the self-styled 'Kolacky Capital of the World.'
entries.dateRule: Late July each year; announced by local organizers.

dates.source: No organizer page could be opened

entries.whatItMarks: Czech heritage and the kolacky pastry.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Royalty in kroje (Czech folk dress); the town also holds a Czech May Day with a maypole and a KCHK radio tent (May 2025).

sources.title: Montgomery Kolacky Days royalty honor Czech heritage, Minnesota Prairie Roots

entries.name: Dožínky (New Prague)
entries.capsule: New Prague's Czech harvest festival with a Main Street parade, run by the Chamber of Commerce; its 40th year was 2024.
entries.dateRule: A September weekend, announced each year by the New Prague Chamber of Commerce.

dates.source: No organizer page could be opened

entries.whatItMarks: Czech harvest traditions and the town's businesses.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Friday car show and concert; Saturday opening ceremony at the Czech Heritage Village, then a noon parade down Main Street (2024).

sources.title: The 40th Dožínky festival, KEYC

entries.name: Burns Night
entries.capsule: Scottish celebration of poet Robert Burns; Mapleton's Burns event dates to 1857 and reached its 143rd in 2019.
entries.dateRule: Around January 25 (Burns's birthday); local dates vary.

dates.source: Traditional date; no Minnesota organizer page opened

entries.whatItMarks: The life and work of Robert Burns and Scottish heritage.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Mapleton's Scots first honored Burns in 1857 and have held a Burns event nearly every year since; St. Andrew's and Caledonian societies in St. Paul, Minneapolis and Duluth held Burns suppers in the 1800s.

sources.title: Scottish Cultural Organizations in Minnesota, MNopedia

entries.name: St. Olaf Christmas Festival
entries.capsule: Century-old choral Christmas festival at St. Olaf College in Northfield, rooted in Norwegian Lutheran music.
entries.dateRule: An early-December weekend, announced each year by St. Olaf College.

dates.source: 2026 dates not shown on the page opened

entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Five choirs and an orchestra in concerts begun by F. Melius Christiansen; the 2025 festival was held Dec. 5-7 and recorded.

sources.title: St. Olaf Christmas Festival, St. Olaf College
